children: Nvidia's expectation-beating quarterly earnings provide short-term relief, but negative forces weighing on the AI trade remain, J.P. Morgan's Sandeep Deshpande and Craig A McDowell write. "The issues the market is concerned about are not really addressed in Nvidia results," the analysts write. Investors are worried about a slowdown in demand for data-center compute following fresh U.S. restrictions on exports to China, they say. A new rule requiring data-center customers in Asia to receive a license from the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced chips also weighs on sentiment, they say. Moreover, cloud-computing companies' financing and domestic U.S. politics provide additional headwinds--all concerns that Nvidia alone can't answer, they say. Nvidia shares rise 3.5% premarket. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
